topic.angle: A labour shortage changed the balance of power

body.claim: After the Black Death, workers were so scarce that wages soared.
body.why: The plague of 1346-1353 shrank the population, and the resulting labour shortage pushed wages up. In some places rents collapsed: one record says a letting that once brought in £5 now brought only £1. Landowners swapped labour services for money rents to keep their tenants. It was not a win for everyone, though: people living on wages alone often lost out to rampant inflation.

probes.question: What happened to wages after the Black Death cut the population?
options: They fell, because there was less work
They rose, because workers were scarce
They were fixed by landowners at one price

probes.question: True or false: landowners offered money rents in place of labour services to keep their tenants.
